title: Week 3, part 2 · From embeddings to BERT

cues.text: Part two: what each neural step fixed, and where it still fails.
An embedding table turns a word I D into a learned row of numbers. The I D itself carries no meaning.
Word2Vec learns the rows from raw text. CBOW predicts the center word from its neighbours. Skip-gram predicts the neighbours from the center.
FastText builds a word from character pieces, so a rare Turkish form like evler still gets a vector.
But averaging word vectors loses order again: dog bites man and man bites dog have the same mean.
A CNN slides a small filter over windows of words.
Each window: multiply, add up, and apply ReLU. Not very gives two, very good gives one, good today gives zero.
Seven tokens with a width of three give seven minus three plus one: five windows.
Max pooling keeps only the strongest response, zero point nine five, and throws away where it was.
An RNN reads one token at a time and carries a hidden state forward.
Because the state depends on order, one then minus one ends negative, and minus one then one ends positive. A mean could not tell them apart.
The problem: training multiplies many derivatives. Twenty factors of zero point five vanish to almost nothing. Twenty factors of one point five explode.
An LSTM adds gates and a cell. The new cell keeps zero point eight of the old one and writes zero point two five of the candidate: zero point four minus zero point one, so zero point three.
A BiLSTM reads both ways and joins them: two hundred fifty-six plus two hundred fifty-six gives five hundred twelve features, for the same number of tokens.
Attention lets every token look at every other token directly.
Scores zero, log two, zero. Softmax: exponentiate to one, two, one, and divide by four. The weights are a quarter, a half, a quarter.
The output mixes the value vectors with those weights: one, two point five.
Padding gets a score of minus infinity, so its weight becomes zero, and the rest are renormalized to one third and two thirds.
Scores are divided by the square root of d k, so the softmax does not get too sharp. For BERT base that is the square root of sixty-four: eight.
BERT is a stack of these attention blocks that reads in both directions.
Each input position adds three vectors: token, segment and position.
It is pretrained by hiding a word, the film was mask, and predicting it. If the right word gets probability one quarter, the loss is log four.
Then a small head is fine-tuned on labeled reviews.
Its limit: a fixed length. Cut a long review at one hundred twenty-eight tokens, and the decisive ending is gone before attention can see it.
Finally, measure it properly. Thirty true positives, five false positives, ten false negatives, fifty-five true negatives.
Precision: thirty out of thirty-five predicted positives. Recall: thirty out of forty real positives.
F1 is two T P over two T P plus F P plus F N: sixty over seventy-five, zero point eight.
Macro F1 averages the class scores: zero point eight and zero point eight eight give zero point eight four.
And always check the majority baseline: always negative already gets sixty percent accuracy.
